title: 04 Synthesis
text:
This notebook draws the PRISMA flow diagram from data/processed/screening_counts.yaml and summarizes the charted sources from data/processed/included_sources_clean.csv. It saves the diagram as data/processed/prisma_flow.png.
The diagram follows the PRISMA 2020 template (Page et al. 2021), with “sources of evidence” in place of “studies” as PRISMA-ScR uses the term (Tricco et al. 2018). Records from other methods are deduplicated against the database records and screened in the same pass, so the diagram shows one path.

from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.ticker import MaxNLocator
import pandas as pd
import yaml
from matplotlib.patches import FancyBboxPatch

ROOT = next(p for p in [Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents] if (p / "_quarto.yml").exists())
OUT = ROOT / "data" / "processed"

counts_path = OUT / "screening_counts.yaml"
counts = (yaml.safe_load(counts_path.read_text()) or {}) if counts_path.exists() else {}

title: 04 Synthesis
text:
Flow diagram


Code
def wrap(lines, width=34):
    out = []
    for line in lines:
        out.extend(textwrap.wrap(line, width) or [""])
    return out


def box_height(lines):
    return 0.30 * len(lines) + 0.35


def draw_box(ax, cx, cy, lines, width):
    h = box_height(lines)
    ax.add_patch(FancyBboxPatch(
        (cx - width / 2, cy - h / 2), width, h,
        boxstyle="round,pad=0.02,rounding_size=0.08", fc="white", ec="black", lw=1,
    ))
    ax.text(cx, cy, "\n".join(lines), ha="center", va="center", fontsize=9, linespacing=1.4)
    return h


def arrow(ax, start, end):
    ax.annotate("", xy=end, xytext=start, arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-|>", lw=1, color="black"))


def flow_rows(c):
    ident, scr, inc = c["identification"], c["screening"], c["included"]
    dbs, others = ident.get("databases", []), ident.get("other_methods", [])
    total = sum(d["n"] for d in dbs) + sum(d["n"] for d in others)
    first = ["Records identified", f"(n = {total})"]
    first += [f"{d['name']}{' [' + d['block'] + ']' if d.get('block') else ''} (n = {d['n']})" for d in dbs]
    first += [f"other: {d['name']} (n = {d['n']})" for d in others]
    removed = [
        "Records removed before screening",
        f"Duplicate records removed (n = {ident.get('duplicates_removed', 0)})",
        f"Marked ineligible by automation tools (n = {ident.get('marked_ineligible_by_automation', 0)})",
        f"Removed for other reasons (n = {ident.get('removed_other_reasons', 0)})",
    ]
    reasons = scr.get("reports_excluded", [])
    excl_total = sum(r["n"] for r in reasons)
    return [
        (first, removed),
        (["Records screened", f"(n = {scr['records_screened']})"], ["Records excluded", f"(n = {scr['records_excluded']})"]),
        (["Reports sought for retrieval", f"(n = {scr['reports_sought']})"], ["Reports not retrieved", f"(n = {scr['reports_not_retrieved']})"]),
        (["Reports assessed for eligibility", f"(n = {scr['reports_assessed']})"],
         ["Reports excluded", f"(n = {excl_total})"] + [f"{r['reason']} (n = {r['n']})" for r in reasons]),
        (["Sources of evidence included in the review", f"(n = {inc['sources']})",
          "Reports of included sources", f"(n = {inc['reports']})"], None),
    ]


def draw_flow(c, path):
    rows = [(wrap(m), wrap(s, 38) if s else None) for m, s in flow_rows(c)]
    main_w, side_w, gap = 4.4, 5.0, 0.8
    x_main, x_side = 3.0, 9.0
    heights = [max(box_height(m), box_height(s) if s else 0) for m, s in rows]
    total = sum(heights) + gap * (len(rows) - 1) + 1
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(13.2 * 0.7, total * 0.7))
    ax.set_xlim(-1.2, 12)
    ax.set_ylim(0, total)
    ax.set_aspect("equal")
    ax.axis("off")
    y, previous, centers = total - 0.5, None, []
    for (m, s), h in zip(rows, heights):
        cy = y - h / 2
        mh = draw_box(ax, x_main, cy, m, main_w)
        if previous:
            arrow(ax, previous, (x_main, cy + mh / 2))
        if s:
            draw_box(ax, x_side, cy, s, side_w)
            arrow(ax, (x_main + main_w / 2, cy), (x_side - side_w / 2, cy))
        previous = (x_main, cy - mh / 2)
        centers.append((cy, h))
        y -= h + gap
    for label, (a, b) in {"Identification": (0, 0), "Screening": (1, 3), "Included": (4, 4)}.items():
        top = centers[a][0] + centers[a][1] / 2
        bottom = centers[b][0] - centers[b][1] / 2
        ax.plot([-0.4, -0.4], [bottom, top], color="black", lw=1)
        ax.text(-0.8, (top + bottom) / 2, label, rotation=90, ha="center", va="center", fontsize=10, fontweight="bold")
    fig.savefig(path, dpi=200, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.show()


if have_flow:
    draw_flow(counts, OUT / "prisma_flow.png")

title: 02 Screening
text:
This notebook reads the title and abstract decisions and the full-text decisions exported from the screening tool, checks them against the deduplicated records, and counts the sources at each stage. It adds the screening, included, and by_block sections to data/processed/screening_counts.yaml. 04 Synthesis draws the flow diagram from that file.
The export formats are in the screening guide. A record is a title and abstract. A report is a full-text document. A source of evidence can have several reports.
Code
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd
import yaml

ROOT = next(p for p in [Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents] if (p / "_quarto.yml").exists())
PROC = ROOT / "data" / "processed"
EXP = ROOT / "data" / "raw" / "screening_exports"
dedup_path = PROC / "deduplicated_records.csv"
ta_path = EXP / "title_abstract.csv"
ft_path = EXP / "full_text.csv"
counts_path = PROC / "screening_counts.yaml"

missing = [str(p.relative_to(ROOT)) for p in (dedup_path, ta_path) if not p.exists()]
have_data = not missing
if not have_data:
    print("Not run yet. Missing: " + ", ".join(missing))


def read(path, required, optional=()):
    df = pd.read_csv(path, dtype=str).fillna("")
    df.columns = [c.strip().lower() for c in df.columns]
    absent = [c for c in required if c not in df.columns]
    if absent:
        raise ValueError(f"{path.name} is missing column(s): {', '.join(absent)}")
    for c in optional:
        if c not in df.columns:
            df[c] = ""
    return df.apply(lambda s: s.str.strip())

title: Research Protocol
text:
Background
Panhuis et al. (2014) reviewed barriers to sharing routinely collected public health data. They defined public health data as data collected by public health agencies for routine purposes, such as disease surveillance or program monitoring, without a primary intention of research. They excluded studies of clinical data and research data. They identified 20 barriers and grouped them into technical, motivational, economic, political, legal, and ethical categories.
Health data fall into two groups with different governance concerns. Health systems data, which include public health data, are collected for operational and administrative purposes. Research data are collected for research under ethics oversight. This review addresses the second group.
Research data sharing has been reviewed across disciplines (Fecher et al. 2015; Zuiderwijk et al. 2020; Perrier et al. 2020). In health and medical research, reviews cover incentives (Rowhani-Farid et al. 2017) and principles and norms (Kalkman et al. 2019), and work on governance mechanisms includes harmonized data access agreements (Saulnier et al. 2019). Several scoping and systematic reviews overlap with parts of this question. The known-item list names them, and the closest is a scoping review of stakeholders’ perceptions of personal health data sharing.
This review also serves the CITF-emails study. It began as an effort to replicate and update Panhuis et al. (2014) in order to derive a taxonomy for manual annotation, which supports supervised machine learning on the emails. A review of research data sharing identifies the full range of factors that the emails cover only in part. It also allows health research data sharing to be compared with data sharing in general and in other fields.

title: Research Protocol
text:
Objective and questions
The objective is to map the factors reported to influence the sharing and reuse of research data in health research, and to compare them with the factors reported for other fields and for public health data.

Which factors (barriers, facilitators, and governance mechanisms) are reported to influence the sharing and reuse of research data in health research?
How can these factors be organized into a taxonomy suitable for annotating correspondence about data sharing?
How do the factors reported for health research differ from those reported for research in other fields?
How do they differ from the barriers that Panhuis et al. (2014) reported for public health data?

title: Research Protocol
text:
Methods
The review follows the scoping review framework of Arksey and O’Malley (2005) as refined by Levac et al. (2010) and the JBI guidance (Peters et al. 2020). It is reported according to PRISMA-ScR (Tricco et al. 2018). The searches are reported according to PRISMA-S (Rethlefsen et al. 2021). The flow diagram adapts the PRISMA 2020 template (Page et al. 2021), with “sources of evidence” in place of “studies”.

Eligibility criteria
The criteria follow the population, concept, and context (PCC) structure that JBI recommends for scoping reviews.







Element
Criterion




Population
No restriction. Sources may concern researchers, data stewards, institutions, or governance bodies.


Concept
Factors that influence the sharing and reuse of research data, including barriers, facilitators, and governance mechanisms. Research data are data collected for research purposes.


Context, tier 1
Health research. All source types are eligible.


Context, tier 2
Research in other fields and cross-disciplinary research. Reviews and syntheses only.



Sources are excluded when they concern only public health data or other health systems data, or only clinical care data. The rule for routine or clinical data reused for research is not yet set. Each source is assigned a tier at screening from its field, so a health review retrieved by either search block is tier 1.
Language and date limits are not yet set. Any limit will be stated and justified, as PRISMA-S item 9 requires.


Information sources and search
Two search blocks run in the same databases. Block A combines research data sharing terms with health terms and applies no source-type limit. Block B combines research data sharing terms with a review filter and applies no health terms. The query terms of Panhuis et al. (2014) are the starting point for the factor terms.
Citation searching of the included sources and of Panhuis et al. (2014) supplements the database searches. Before the full searches run, the final strings are tested against a list of known relevant sources. The databases are not yet selected. Every search is recorded on the search strategy page.


Selection of sources
Search results are deduplicated and then screened on title and abstract, and again on full text, against the screening guide. Exclusion reasons are recorded at full text. Counts at every stage feed the flow diagram.


Data charting
Each included source is charted once into the form defined in the codebook. The form is piloted on a sample of sources and revised before full charting begins.


Synthesis
Factors are coded to categories that start from the six categories of Panhuis et al. (2014) and are revised inductively. The resulting taxonomy is a primary output. Counts by tier, field, source type, and year describe the evidence base, and the factor categories are compared across fields.


Reporting and data
The checklists for PRISMA-ScR and PRISMA-S record where each item is reported. The flow diagram is generated from the screening counts. Search exports, screening decisions, charted data, and all code are in the repository.

title: Research Protocol

Open decisions

Databases and platforms.
Language and date limits.
The rule for routine or clinical data reused for research.
The definition of research data, by purpose or by consent.
The number of screeners, calibration on a sample, and the handling of disagreement.
Critical appraisal of included sources, which PRISMA-ScR treats as optional.
Whether any step uses a large language model. Any such step will be reported following the PRISMA 2020 guidance on automation tools and the RAISE guidance.

title: Screening guide
text: The guide states how records are screened and how decisions are exported for the analysis notebooks. The criteria come from the protocol and are a draft.

title: Screening guide
text:
Stages

Title and abstract. Each deduplicated record gets one decision, include or exclude. When the title and abstract do not allow a decision, include the record.
Full text. Each included record’s full text is retrieved. A report that cannot be retrieved is counted as not retrieved. Each retrieved report gets one decision, and each exclusion gets one reason from the list below.

Each included report is assigned to a source of evidence. Reports of the same study share one source_id.

title: Screening guide
text:
Criteria
A source is included when all of these hold.

It concerns the sharing or reuse of research data.
It reports factors that influence sharing or reuse, including barriers, facilitators, and governance mechanisms.
It concerns health research (tier 1), or it is a review or synthesis of research in other fields or across fields (tier 2).

A source is excluded when it concerns only public health data, other health systems data, or only clinical care data. The rule for routine or clinical data reused for research is not yet set.

title: Research data sharing: a scoping review (RDS-Review)
text:
RDS-Review maps the factors reported to influence the sharing and reuse of research data, including barriers, facilitators, and governance mechanisms. It centres on health research data and compares it with research data sharing in other fields.
The review began as an effort to replicate and update the systematic review by Panhuis et al. (2014) of barriers to sharing public health data. That review defined public health data as data collected by public health agencies for routine purposes, and it excluded studies of research data. This review takes research data as its subject. The taxonomy of factors it produces will support manual annotation for supervised machine learning in the CITF-emails study. The review also identifies factors that the emails cover only in part, and it allows health research data sharing to be compared with data sharing in general and in other fields.






NoteStatus



Draft protocol. The protocol is not yet registered, and the eligibility criteria, databases, and limits can still change. See the Research Protocol.


This website hosts the research protocol, the codebook, the search and screening materials, and the notebooks that turn search exports and screening decisions into counts, tables, and the PRISMA flow diagram. All content is hosted and tracked at github.com/zackbatist/RDS-Review.

title: Analysis
text: Four notebooks turn the raw files into counts, tables, and figures. Each reads from data/raw/ or data/processed/ and writes only to data/processed/. No notebook changes a raw file. Deleting data/processed/ and rerunning the notebooks in order rebuilds it.

title: Analysis
text:
Running
Install Quarto and the Python packages in requirements.txt. Then render one notebook at a time, in order, as data arrives.
quarto render analysis/01-deduplication.ipynb
The site is set to freeze: true, so a full quarto render reuses the stored results in _freeze/ and does not rerun the notebooks. After the data change, render the affected notebooks explicitly. Commit _freeze/ so the site builds without rerunning them.

title: Codebook
text:
The codebook defines the charting form. It lists every variable charted for each included source of evidence, as PRISMA-ScR item 11 requires. The form is a draft and will be revised after piloting on a sample of sources.
Each source is one row in data/raw/included_sources_raw.csv. Variables that take several values hold them in one cell, separated by semicolons. Closed variables take only the values listed below, in lowercase.



Variable
Definition
Allowed values




source_id
Identifier of the source of evidence. Reports of the same study share one source_id.
Free text


record_id
Identifier of the primary report in deduplicated_records.csv.
Free text


tier
Context tier from the protocol.
1, 2


field
Field of research the source concerns.
health, other, cross-disciplinary


field_detail
Specific field or subfield, such as genomics or archaeology.
Free text


source_type
Type of source.
empirical, review, policy-guidance, opinion, other


peer_reviewed
Whether the source was peer reviewed.
yes, no


data_origin
Origin of the data the source concerns. research means collected for research. routine-reused means collected for operational or care purposes and reused for research.
research, routine-reused, mixed, unclear


factor_types
Kinds of factor the source reports.
barrier, facilitator, governance-mechanism


factor_categories
Initial categories from Panhuis et al. (2014), revised during synthesis.
technical, motivational, economic, political, legal, ethical, other


level
Level at which the factor operates. system covers national, sectoral, and international levels.
individual, institutional, system


factors
The specific factors the source reports, in the source’s words or a close paraphrase.
Free text, semicolon-separated


region
Country or region of the data, institutions, or participants.
Free text


notes
Anything that affects interpretation.
Free text



03-charting.ipynb checks charted values against the closed lists above and reports any value that is not allowed. The lists are written in that notebook as well, so a change here needs the same change there.

Known-item test
Before the full searches run, the final strings are tested against these sources. The first two groups are in scope, so both blocks together should retrieve them. The last two groups are comparators or adjacent work, and retrieving them is not required.

Export file names
Name each export <database>_<YYYY-MM-DD>[_<block>].<ext>, for example scopus_2026-11-02_A.ris. The date is the search date. Supported formats are RIS and CSV. See the README in data/raw/search_exports/.

if have_data:
    path = OUT / "screening_counts.yaml"
    counts = (yaml.safe_load(path.read_text()) or {}) if path.exists() else {}
    previous = counts.get("identification", {})
    is_other = by_export["database"].str.startswith("other-")

    def entry(r, strip=False):
        name = r.database.removeprefix("other-") if strip else r.database
        return {"name": name, "block": r.block or None, "search_date": r.search_date, "n": int(r.records)}

    counts["identification"] = {
        "databases": [entry(r) for r in by_export[~is_other].itertuples()],
        "other_methods": [entry(r, strip=True) for r in by_export[is_other].itertuples()],
        "duplicates_removed": int(total - unique),
        "marked_ineligible_by_automation": previous.get("marked_ineligible_by_automation", 0),
        "removed_other_reasons": previous.get("removed_other_reasons", 0),
    }
    path.write_text(yaml.safe_dump(counts, sort_keys=False))
    print("Wrote data/processed/screening_counts.yaml")

title: 03 Charting
text:
This notebook cleans the charted data in data/raw/included_sources_raw.csv and checks it against the codebook. It writes data/processed/included_sources_clean.csv and data/processed/bibliography.csv, which holds the reference details of each included source, taken from the deduplicated records.
Cleaning trims whitespace, lowercases the closed variables, and sorts and deduplicates the values of the multi-valued variables. A value outside the allowed lists is reported and left as entered.
Code
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

ROOT = next(p for p in [Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents] if (p / "_quarto.yml").exists())
RAW = ROOT / "data" / "raw" / "included_sources_raw.csv"
DEDUP = ROOT / "data" / "processed" / "deduplicated_records.csv"
OUT = ROOT / "data" / "processed"

COLUMNS = [
    "source_id", "record_id", "tier", "field", "field_detail", "source_type",
    "peer_reviewed", "data_origin", "factor_types", "factor_categories",
    "level", "factors", "region", "notes",
]
REQUIRED = ["source_id", "record_id", "tier", "field", "source_type"]

# These lists mirror codebook.qmd. Change both together.
SINGLE = {
    "tier": ["1", "2"],
    "field": ["health", "other", "cross-disciplinary"],
    "source_type": ["empirical", "review", "policy-guidance", "opinion", "other"],
    "peer_reviewed": ["yes", "no"],
    "data_origin": ["research", "routine-reused", "mixed", "unclear"],
}
MULTI = {
    "factor_types": ["barrier", "facilitator", "governance-mechanism"],
    "factor_categories": ["technical", "motivational", "economic", "political", "legal", "ethical", "other"],
    "level": ["individual", "institutional", "system"],
}

raw = pd.read_csv(RAW, dtype=str).fillna("") if RAW.exists() else pd.DataFrame(columns=COLUMNS)
absent = [c for c in COLUMNS if c not in raw.columns]
if absent:
    raise ValueError("included_sources_raw.csv is missing column(s): " + ", ".join(absent))
have_data = len(raw) > 0
print(f"{len(raw)} charted source(s)." if have_data else "No charted sources yet. Add rows to data/raw/included_sources_raw.csv.")


No charted sources yet. Add rows to data/raw/included_sources_raw.csv.
Code
if have_data:
    clean = raw[COLUMNS].apply(lambda s: s.str.strip())
    for col in SINGLE:
        clean[col] = clean[col].str.lower()

    def tidy(cell):
        values = [v.strip().lower() for v in cell.split(";") if v.strip()]
        return "; ".join(sorted(set(values)))

    for col in MULTI:
        clean[col] = clean[col].map(tidy)
